messages.text: Yes but how does miners work with app

I'm Hal, HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Happy to explain.

Most of our home miners (Bitaxe, NerdQX, NerdOctaxe and similar) don't need a special app. Your phone works as the remote control:

1. **First setup:** when you power the miner on for the first time, it creates its own Wi-Fi network. Join it from your phone and a setup page opens. There you enter your home Wi-Fi and the pool address.
2. **Daily use:** once it's on your Wi-Fi, the miner shows its IP address on its little screen. Type that address into your phone's browser to open its dashboard. It shows your hashrate, temperature, fan speed and best share, and you can change settings there too.
3. **Earnings:** if you mine in a pool, you check your sats on the pool's website or app. If you mine solo, the dashboard shows your "best difficulty", which tells you how close you've come to finding a block.

One catch: your phone has to be on the same Wi-Fi as the miner to open the dashboard.

Did you have a particular app or miner in mind? Tell me which one and I'll explain how it works with it.
If I have mobile Hotspot will it work with that

Yes, a phone hotspot usually works for our small Wi-Fi miners (Bitaxe, NerdQX, NerdOctaxe). Check these first:

1. **Use 2.4 GHz.** These miners only connect to 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi. On an iPhone, turn on "Maximize Compatibility" in the Personal Hotspot settings. On Android, set the hotspot band to 2.4 GHz.
2. **Keep the phone on and nearby.** If the hotspot turns off or the phone moves out of range, the miner stops mining until it reconnects.
3. **Check your data plan.** Mining uses very little data, but it runs all day and night. Make sure your carrier allows hotspot use and doesn't cut or slow it after a limit.

To open the miner's dashboard, type the IP address shown on its screen into your phone's browser.

Which miner are you looking at? Bigger units can work differently, so I'll check that one for you.

What is name miner can I use with my mobile Hotspot

These miners connect over Wi-Fi, so they work with a phone hotspot set to 2.4 GHz:

1. **Bitaxe:** the smallest and quietest. A good first miner for lottery (solo) mining at home.
2. **NerdQX:** more hashing power than a Bitaxe, so better odds, but more heat and fan noise.
3. **NerdOctaxe:** the most power of the three, with more heat and noise to match.

All three set up the same way: join the miner's own Wi-Fi from your phone, enter your hotspot name and password, then point it at a pool.

For the bigger miners in our shop, I'd want to check their connection options before saying they'll work on a hotspot. Tell me if one of them interests you.

Does a small, quiet miner suit you, or do you want the most hashing power for your money?
